title: Amine Preparations: Gabriel Phthalimide & Hofmann Bromamide Degradation
topics: 3. Amine Preparative Routes Overview (Nitrile Reduction, Mendius Reduction via Na/EtOH)
3.1 Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis (Pure 1° Aliphatic Amines via Potassium Phthalimide and R-X S_N2)
CRITICAL NEST LIMITATION: Inability to Synthesize Aniline via Gabriel Phthalimide (Aryl Halides fail S_N2)
3.2 Hofmann Bromamide Degradation Reaction (RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH ──► RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O)
Mechanistic Cascade: N-Bromoamide ──► Acyl Nitrene ──► 1,2-Alkyl Shift to Isocyanate (R-N=C=O) ──► Hydrolysis
Loss of 1 Carbon Atom & Stereochemical Retention at Chiral Migrating Center
quickSummary: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis yields pure 1° aliphatic amines via S_N2 substitution; aromatic amines (Aniline) CANNOT be made because aryl halides do not undergo S_N2. Hofmann bromamide degradation converts primary amides to 1° amines with ONE LESS CARBON via an acyl nitrene, 1,2-alkyl shift to isocyanate (R-N=C=O), and hydrolysis (4 moles of NaOH consumed per mole of amide).
summary: Master Gabriel phthalimide synthesis constraints and the step-by-step Hofmann bromamide degradation cascade.

summaryBox.title: Gabriel Phthalimide Scope
summaryBox.takeaway: Yields pure 1° aliphatic amines without 2°/3° contamination. CANNOT synthesize Aniline because aryl halides fail S_N2 substitution with phthalimide anion.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GABRIEL PHTHALIMIDE MECHANISM
                    
   Phthalimide ──[KOH]──► Potassium Phthalimide ──[R-X ($S_N2$)]──► N-Alkylphthalimide
                                                                            │
   $1^\circ$ Aliphatic Amine ($R\text{-NH}_2$) + Phthalate Salt ◄──[aq. NaOH / $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$ Hydrolysis]┘
conceptBreakdown.content: Phthalimide is deprotonated by $\text{KOH}$ to potassium phthalimide, which undergoes an $S_N2$ displacement on an alkyl halide ($R\text{-X}$) to form $N$-alkylphthalimide, hydrolyzed to yield a pure primary aliphatic amine.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 3.2 Hofmann Bromamide Degradation Mechanism
conceptBreakdown.title: 3.2 Hofmann Bromamide Degradation Mechanism
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
HOFMANN BROMAMIDE MECHANISTIC CASCADE
                    
   $R\text{-CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{OH}^-} R\text{-CONH-Br} \xrightarrow{\text{-H}^+} R\text{-C(O)-\bar{N}-Br} \xrightarrow{-\text{Br}^-} [R\text{-C(O)-\ddot{N}:} \text{ Nitrene}]$
                                                                                         │
   $R\text{-NH}_2 \text{ (Amine with 1 C less!)} \longleftarrow \text{Hydrolysis} \longleftarrow R\text{-N=C=O (Isocyanate)} \xleftarrow{\mathbf{1,2-\text{Alkyl Shift}}}$

Overall: RCONH₂ + Br₂ + 4NaOH ──► RNH₂ + Na₂CO₃ + 2NaBr + 2H₂O
conceptBreakdown.content: Primary amides react with $\text{Br}_2$ and $4\text{ NaOH}$ to yield a $1^\circ$ primary amine containing **one carbon less** than the starting amide. The intramolecular 1,2-shift occurs with complete retention of configuration at migrating chiral centers.

quickRevision: Gabriel synthesis yields pure 1° aliphatic amines (S_N2).
Gabriel synthesis CANNOT prepare Aniline (Ar-X fails S_N2).
Hofmann degradation yields 1° amine with 1 less carbon.
Consumes 4 moles of NaOH per mole of primary amide.
Proceeds via Nitrene and Isocyanate (R-N=C=O) with stereochemical retention.
